title: UGC Commerce Video Storyboard Schema
description: Schema for structured short-form ecommerce storyboard planning output.

task_type.description: Fixed task type for this schema.

summary.description: Top-level summary of the storyboard and its commercial purpose.

storyboard_objective.description: Primary business or communication objective of the video.

core_angle.description: Central creative angle of the storyboard.

recommended_format.description: Suggested visual format such as UGC demo, testimonial, comparison, routine integration, or showcase.

main_promise.description: Primary product promise communicated by the storyboard.

proof_strategy.description: How the storyboard visually proves the promise.

cta_goal.description: Intended next action for the viewer.

structure_type.description: Narrative or selling structure such as hook-product-demo-proof-cta or pain-solution-proof-cta.

flow_summary.description: High-level summary of how the scenes progress.

product_reveal_timing.description: When the product becomes clearly visible.

cta_position.description: Where the CTA lands in the sequence.

purpose.description: Commercial function of the scene such as hook, product intro, demo, proof, objection handling, or CTA.

viewer_takeaway.description: What the viewer should understand, feel, or believe after this scene.

visual_description.description: Detailed description of what should appear on screen.

product_visibility_note.description: How clearly and prominently the product should be shown.

spoken_line_or_message.description: Recommended spoken line, narration, or core message.

overlay_text.description: Suggested on-screen text or subtitle emphasis.

proof_role.description: How this scene contributes proof or credibility.

objection_role.description: If relevant, what hesitation this scene helps reduce.

camera_framing.description: Suggested framing such as close-up, medium shot, macro detail, POV, or over-the-shoulder.

camera_motion.description: Suggested motion such as static, handheld, push-in, reveal pan, or quick cut.

transition_note.description: How the scene should connect to the next one.

hook_scene_plan.description: Special planning layer for the opening scene or first few seconds.

hook_scene_number.description: Scene number containing the primary hook.

hook_type.description: Type of hook such as pain, result, comparison, identity, curiosity, or surprise.

hook_visual_strategy.description: What visual pattern makes the opening likely to stop the scroll.

mute_viewing_support.description: How the hook remains understandable without audio.

product_visibility_plan.description: How product clarity is maintained across the storyboard.

first_clear_product_scene.description: Scene where the product first becomes clearly understandable.

visibility_priority_note.description: What must be visually clear about the product.

usage_clarity_note.description: How the viewer learns how the product is used.

repeat_visibility_strategy.description: How the product continues to stay present and legible throughout the video.

proof_plan.description: Visual proof design layer for the storyboard.

proof_scenes.description: Scene numbers or labels where proof appears.

proof_priority_note.description: What absolutely must be shown to make the storyboard convincing.

proof_risk_note.description: What may feel unconvincing if proof is too weak or unclear.

objection_handling_plan.description: How the storyboard visually or verbally reduces hesitation.

handling_scenes.description: Scene numbers or labels where objection handling occurs.

handling_method.description: How the storyboard responds to the objection.

overlay_and_subtitle_plan.description: Plan for text support in the video.

overlay_strategy.description: How overlays support comprehension, proof, or CTA.

priority_overlay_moments.description: Scene numbers or messages where text is most important.

density_note.description: Guidance on how much text should appear at once.

avoid_note.description: What to avoid in text treatment, such as clutter or repetition.

pacing_and_transition_plan.description: Guidance on energy, rhythm, and scene flow.

fast_moments.description: Scenes or moments that should move quickly.

slow_moments.description: Scenes or moments that should breathe for clarity or proof.

transition_style.description: General transition behavior such as hard cuts, soft continuity, punchy jumps, or proof-led progression.

momentum_note.description: How pacing supports retention and understanding.

cta_ending_plan.description: How the ending should visually support the CTA.

ending_scene_number.description: Scene number containing the main CTA ending.

ending_visual.description: What the viewer sees during the CTA moment.

cta_type.description: CTA style such as direct action, benefit-led, urgency-led, or trust-led.

action_clarity_note.description: How clearly the viewer understands what to do next.

production_notes.description: Practical notes for filming, editing, or generation.

must_capture_shots.description: Essential shots that cannot be omitted.

simplification_opportunities.description: Areas where the storyboard can be simplified if needed.

creator_direction_note.description: How the creator should perform or appear if relevant.

editing_note.description: Key note for edit rhythm, structure, or sequence.

generation_note.description: If AI generation is the next step, note what should remain especially concrete.

assumptions.description: Assumptions made because of incomplete user input.

warnings.description: Risks related to proof, production complexity, or product clarity.

next_steps.description: Suggested follow-up actions such as script refinement, prompt conversion, or asset generation.
